title: Practitioner Exam
description: DRAFT for review - generated from the course content; review and refine in the Question Bank app before a real workshop. 15 questions per attempt from a pool of 18, pass mark 80%.

questions.prompt: Which Pentaho design tool is the most comprehensive report authoring tool in the suite?
questions.explanation: Report Designer offers the deepest layout, data, and scripting control of Pentaho's reporting tools; Interactive Reports is the lighter web-based option.
questions.source: Getting Started with Pentaho Business Analytics

questions.prompt: Reports created in Report Designer are saved with which file extension?
questions.explanation: Report Designer saves .prpt files; .prpti is the Interactive Reports format.
questions.source: Getting Started with Pentaho Business Analytics

questions.prompt: The Welcome screen's sample reports only display when what is true?
options: The Pentaho sample data (HSQLDB) database is installed and running
The reports have been published at least once
You are connected to the BA repository
questions.explanation: The samples query the HSQLDB sample database, so it must be running for them to open.

questions.prompt: In Report Designer, where do you switch to a preview of the report output?
options: The eye icon on the formatting toolbar
questions.explanation: The eye icon on the formatting toolbar toggles preview mode; the Preview toolbar then offers print, navigation, and zoom.

questions.prompt: Which data source type would you choose to query a relational database directly with SQL?
questions.explanation: JDBC connects to relational databases and runs SQL; Metadata uses an XMI model, Pentaho Analysis a Mondrian schema, XML an XQuery file.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which of these are data source types Report Designer understands?
questions.explanation: Report Designer supports JDBC, Metadata, Pentaho Analysis, XML, tables, and the Sequence Generator - not office documents.

questions.prompt: Where are report elements placed in Report Designer?
options: Inside bands (report header, group header, details, footers)
Directly on the page with absolute pixel coordinates only
questions.explanation: The canvas is organised into horizontal bands; elements live inside them and repeat according to the band's role.
questions.source: Adding Report Elements and Creating Groups

questions.prompt: What does adding a group to a report do?
options: Gathers detail rows that share a value into sections with their own header and footer bands
Sorts the query without changing layout
Restricts which users can run the report
questions.explanation: Groups turn flat rows into structured sections - e.g. one section per Product Line - each with header/footer bands for labels and totals.
questions.source: Adding Report Elements and Creating Groups

questions.prompt: How is conditional formatting driven in Report Designer?
options: By attaching a formula to a style property of an element
By a setting in the publish dialog
questions.explanation: A formula on a style property evaluates per row and changes the element's appearance with the data.

questions.prompt: To show a running total for a group, you would typically add what?
options: A function from the Data tab placed in the group footer
A sub-report in the details band
A parameter with a default value
questions.explanation: Predefined functions (sum, count, running totals) are added on the Data tab and placed in footer bands to summarise the group.

questions.prompt: Which band would you use for content that must appear at the top of every page?
questions.explanation: The page header repeats on every page; the report header prints once at the start of the report.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a report parameter?
options: To prompt the user for a value at run time and feed it into the query or expressions
questions.explanation: Parameters make one report serve many filters: the user picks values at run time and the data responds.

questions.prompt: After defining a parameter, what must you usually change so it filters the data?
options: The query, to reference the parameter in its WHERE clause
questions.explanation: A parameter only affects the data when the query (or an expression) references it.

questions.prompt: A sub-report is best described as what?
options: A complete report with its own query embedded inside another report
questions.explanation: Sub-reports carry their own data source and layout - the building block for composing several result sets into one report.

questions.prompt: What does making a chart drillable add?
options: A link from chart regions to a more detailed report or view
questions.explanation: Drill-down wires chart elements to a target (another report, URL, or view) so a summary click opens the underlying detail.

questions.prompt: Publishing a report from Report Designer sends it where?
options: To the Pentaho Server's BA repository
To the samples folder on disk
questions.explanation: Publish uploads the .prpt to the BA repository, where users run it from the Pentaho User Console.

questions.prompt: Once published, where do business users typically run the report?
options: The Pentaho User Console in a browser
A local copy of Report Designer
questions.explanation: PUC is the server's browser UI for browsing, running, and scheduling published content.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: hyperlinks in a published report can point to which targets?
questions.explanation: Hyperlinks link elements to other reports, URLs, and drill targets - queries are not link targets.
